items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I worked with people like that; Robert Emmet Dolling was one, and he translated his setting

ctx.x: You mentioned that the other day.

I heard A Little Night Music was that way too. I think you have to give Sondheim his due, and I never know how much goes to the orchestrator and how much goes to composer. It depends really on the guy who does--I use that word advisedly, because most Broadway writers are not composers; they're tunesmiths. There is a huge difference. But Sondheim, not having worked with him, I really don't know. I have a suspicion that he watches his notes carefully.

I worked with people like that; Robert Emmet Dolling was one, and he translated his setting, he made his--even their orchestral settings--we were talking about this sort of thing before, about Hollywood,
